d.a: Distribution. Known only from the type locality, in Trung Trang Cave, on Cat Ba Island in the Gulf of Tonkin, northeastern Vietnam. Notes on habitat. The type locality is a large shallow pool of percolated water in a long tunnel cave located in National in Park on Cat Ba Island; the cave is managed for tourists, but little adapted (Sket, pers. communication). Cat Ba is largest island (140 km 2) in the Cat Ba Archipelago, in the world-famous Ha Long Bay; more than half of the main island is a National Park, which is home to the highly endangered Cat Ba langur — Trachypithecus poliocephalus poliocephalus (Trouessart). Accompanying fauna at the type locality includes a moderately dense population of a tiny stygobiontic bathynellid (Paraeobathynella vietnamensis Camacho), cyclopoid copepods, ostracods, decapods of the genus Tiwaripotamon Bott and gastropods of the genus Systenostoma Bavay and Dautzenberg; insects are represented by larvae of Culicidae and some other Diptera (information provided by Boris Sket).

Distribution. Japan: Honshu (Harukawa, 1919). Korea (Okamoto, 1938). In Japan, this species has been known from western and central Honshu (Harukawa, 1919; Takimoto & Oda, 1940). We found a female collected in Yamagata Prefecture, northern Honshu.
